summary: Tested v72e: partner draft fix (resend/invite-existing/admin edit), consortium settings + criteria consortium fields, full consortium lifecycle (create/invite/limit/decline/accept/terms/sign/upload/remove), consortium bid incl. per-member criteria answers, Stage 2 consortium rules (lead/combined/each), preliminary + final result notices and /results/vendor/mine privacy. Backend: 36/37 pytest pass; 1 real bug found (withdrawn consortium bid deadlocks the consortium and its members). Frontend: Admin Partners draft flow, vendor consortium flow on BidSubmit (form, invite, terms, sign, per-member criteria inputs, real UI bid submission), /vendor/consortia accept+sign, member note on bid page, My bids criteria results all work end-to-end. Two contrast/design bugs in the dark 'E' theme.

critical.issue: When the lead withdraws a consortium bid, the consortium stays status='bid_submitted' (withdraw_bid never touches db.consortia). Result: lead cannot rebid via the consortium (_editable 409 'bid has been submitted'), cannot withdraw the consortium (409), cannot create a new one or bid alone (busy_on_notice treats bid_submitted as live), and every member gets 409 'You are part of a consortium for this tender' when bidding alone. Permanent deadlock on that tender. Reproduced in TestG_WithdrawRelease.

minor.issue: For rule 'each' with numeric operator 'lte', the shown team value is min(nums), which should be max (pass/fail is still right because the per-member 'bad' list is used, but value/scoring for an auto-scored 'each' lte criterion uses the wrong number).
Returns the raw doc incl. agreement signature tokens; strip them like view().
No email/notification to the member who was removed (an accepted member is dropped silently). Also PUT /terms 'shares' accepts arbitrary keys with no validation (unknown vendor ids silently ignored).
Only checks vendor status=='active' and not kyc_status=='verified', although the review request says members need KYC passed.
Snapshot does not store email_sent per recipient, so admins can't see whether the notice email was actually delivered.

issues: Box uses bg-slate-50, which index.css line ~708 globally remaps to dark green under [data-ui="e"]. Computed bg rgb(6,32,26) with text rgb(15,23,42): the heading 'This tender accepts consortium bids', the 'Bid alone' / 'Bid as consortium lead' radio labels and the lead note can't be read (dark on dark). Fix: use bg-white or a custom class, or add [data-ui="e"] [data-testid="bid-consortium"] {background:#F8FAFC !important} like the v51v light-page pins.

Consortium name (text-slate-900), the tender/limit subtitle, the page intro paragraph and the agreement helper text (text-slate-600) show as very faint cream on a light card/page because of the global E-theme slate remaps. Add a light-page override for consortia-list/cons-card-* like the admin-bid-page block in index.css.

Escrow/deposit selects show 'One shared escrow' / 'Lead pays' as if chosen, while the issues list still says 'Choose how escrow and the bid deposit will work' until Save terms is clicked. Add a placeholder option or a 'not saved yet' hint.
entity_type is a free-text input (backend only accepts individual|company). Use a select.
Read-only view hides the consortium section, so admins can't see whether a live tender accepts consortium bids or its member limit.

action_items: HIGH: when a bid that has bid.consortium is withdrawn (bids.py withdraw_bid), set that consortium back to 'forming' (or 'withdrawn') and clear bid_id. Also decide whether busy_on_notice should ignore consortia whose bid was withdrawn. Rerun TestG_WithdrawRelease.
Fix contrast of BidConsortiumBox (bg-slate-50 remapped dark) and of the /vendor/consortia page text (slate-900/600 remapped light) under the E theme.

Minor: _team_value 'each'+'lte' should use max; strip signature tokens in admin_list; tell a removed member they were removed; validate terms.shares keys; think about requiring kyc_status verified for members; turn entity_type into a select in the admin edit form.
critical_code_review_comments: bids.withdraw_bid has no consortium handling (root cause of the HIGH bug).

consortia.busy_on_notice counts 'invited' as busy, so a supplier who is only invited (hasn't accepted) is already blocked from bidding alone. Might be intended, but a lead can lock out any supplier by inviting them. Consider blocking only on 'accepted', or let the invitee decline from the bid page.
bid_opening._open reuses the variable name q for both the Mongo query and the evaluation result. It works because the cursor already exists, but it's fragile.
send_result_notices runs as a fire-and-forget asyncio.create_task after the technical opening. Exceptions are lost, so wrap it in try/except with a log line.

rca of the issue: Withdraw deadlock: consortia.mark_submitted sets status='bid_submitted' (in FINAL). bids.withdraw_bid only updates the bid. FINAL statuses make _editable reject every consortium change including withdraw, and busy_on_notice treats any non-'withdrawn' consortium as live. Repro: form a ready consortium, submit the bid with consortium_id, POST /bids/{id}/withdraw. A member's solo bid then gets 409 and POST /consortia/{id}/withdraw gets 409. Mitigation: in withdraw_bid, if b.consortium, update consortia {_id: b.consortium.id} to status 'forming' and unset bid_id (or 'withdrawn').
